outcomes.evidence: `typo3_project_scope` and `typo3_extension_scope` are the fifth and sixth calls of the session and the first two that touch the repository at all — everything before them is the skill and its two references. All four facts are then operative rather than declared in a header. The declared range is what compatibility is measured against: finding 8 kills a `getMajorVersion() >= 13` branch as "always true given `composer.json` requires `^13.4 || ^14.3`", and finding 5 keeps `addStaticFile()` as "a deliberate v13-compatibility trade-off". Standalone versus installation carries the whole of finding 2 — the element renders in this checkout only because the dev site's sets are `bootstrap-package/full` and `syntax/base`, which `typo3_project_scope` reported and which the answer traces to `lib.contentElement` in bootstrap_package's `ContentElement.typoscript:20`. Repository-owned commands are named where they are the subject: `composer test` resolving through `@test:php:lint` to `phplint`, `cgl:ci` and `test:php:lint` as the two CI steps, `composer set-version` in finding 7 — four of the five `typo3_project_scope` returned. The PHP floor is the one fact never stated in its own right; it appears only as the CI matrix's 8.2–8.5.

Every finding carries a path, most a line, and eleven were re-checked against the checkout while judging this run — all eleven hold, including the four that name the installed core. `PackageManager::isComposerOnlyCapable()` is at 954-960 and does require both `providesPackages` and a version; the deprecation text in finding 7 is quoted verbatim from `PackageManager.php:936-945`; `addStaticFile` is at `ExtensionManagementUtility.php:1013` and `addRecordType` at `:868`; and the v14 backend title really is `explode(' - ', $description, 2)` at `Package.php:149`. In the extension: `setup.typoscript:1` is `tt_content.syntax =< lib.contentElement` with `lib.contentElement` defined nowhere in the repository, `layoutRootPaths.1` and `partialRootPaths.1` point at two directories that do not exist, the four language lists hold 20, 20, 8 and 17 entries, `'sql'` is in the format whitelist and in neither the TCA select nor the Grunt bundle, `RteConfigEnhancer.php:27` is an assignment to `$configuration['codeBlock']` with no guard of any kind above it, `locallang_be.xlf` has five trans-units, and `publish.yml` runs `setup-php` on 7.4 behind a repository-owner gate. Only subsystems the extension has are opened: `typo3_extension_scope` reports no backend modules, routes or middlewares and none are asked for. What is not gathered a third time is a run of anything: not `composer test`, not `cgl:ci`, not `phplint` — the verification findings rest on reading CI and Composer configuration, and the answer does not say so.

All six areas appear and each is anchored. Compatibility: the two-manifest metadata gap that fires `E_USER_DEPRECATED` on every 14.x request path, `addTcaSelectItem` versus `addRecordType`, the dead `isLoaded('t3editor')` branch. Behavioral correctness: the undeclared `lib.contentElement` dependency, the RTE listener rewriting every preset in the installation, Prism CSS and JavaScript on every page of the site. Test evidence: finding 1, that a 2×4 matrix runs two version-independent steps and proves nothing beyond "the files parse". Documentation: `artifacts.manual` null, a three-line README, five untranslated trans-units. Release: the TER-versus-Composer metadata divergence and, in the coverage table, `setup-php` on 7.4 plus a publish job that never asserts the tag matches `ext_emconf.php`. Static quality is the thinnest of the six and is the reason this run was made: php-cs-fixer and phplint are assessed — correctly, as checks that cannot distinguish `^13` from `^14` — but the answer never names static **analysis** as a thing this repository does not have. There is no PHPStan here, no baseline, no analysis step in CI, and none of that is a finding; the gap is folded into "there is no verification layer at all" and remediated with a PHPUnit harness alone.

The order is argued rather than labelled: finding 1 leads because it is "the root cause of items 2, 3 and 5 below going unnoticed", finding 2 follows with the consequence spelled out as "an unreproducible-by-you support ticket" for a consumer who installs the package and gets an element that renders nothing without an exception or a log line. Uncertainty is stated inside the finding it belongs to, not appended: finding 4 records the installation-wide RTE scope as "unestablished intent rather than asserting it is accidental" because the README is three lines and there is no manual; the coverage table reports the trailing comma in `ext_tables.sql` as **not** a defect after test-parsing the file with the core's own `Parser`/`Lexer`, and `setup-php` on 7.4 as a latent risk rather than a break because `typo3/tailor` still declares `php: ^7.2 || ^8.0`. Two of the nine severities are argued against their own headline — "Low, but it is what turns each item above into a ticket" on documentation — which reads as the priority being the order rather than the label. What is missing is the same sentence the two bootstrap_package runs were missing: that no declared command was executed, so findings 1 and 7 are read rather than reproduced.

"Who takes these onward" routes finding 1 to **typo3-extension-testing** with its scope bounded to `Build/` configurations, `Tests/Unit`, `Tests/Functional` and a CI job; findings 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 to **typo3-content-element-development**; finding 9 to **typo3-extension-documentation**; and keeps conformance for the re-check. Finding 7 is explicitly given no skill at all — "a two-key `composer.json` edit". The transcript agrees with the closing sentence: 64 tool calls, 27 Read, 19 Bash, 15 server calls, 2 ToolSearch, 1 Skill, and not one Write, Edit or NotebookEdit. `git status` in the checkout afterwards shows only the ` M .gitignore` and `?? .mcp.json` the install left. The answer ends by offering two starting points and starting neither.

failures.evidence: The coverage table closes what the extension does not have rather than asking for it: no backend modules, no routes, no middlewares, no state-changing requests, no secrets. Two absent things are named as absent and then argued to be acceptable — a backend preview is "a recommendation, not a violation", and `.html` rather than `.fluid.html` is "the documented predecessor form on v14, not a defect". Nothing installation-level is demanded of a distributed package. The one place where a missing file becomes a finding is finding 2, and there it is a file the extension's own TypoScript points at.

Compatibility is measured against the declaration throughout, and the older major is argued for rather than filtered away. Finding 5 keeps `addStaticFile()` and `Configuration/TypoScript/` because "if v13 sites still need the static template", and defers deletion to "when v13 support is dropped". Finding 8 uses the declared range to prove a runtime branch dead rather than reading the installed 14.3.0 as the truth. Finding 1's whole argument is that the declared `^13`/`^14` matrix does not actually exercise either. Where the installed core is used it is used as evidence for a mechanism — `PackageManager`, `ExtensionManagementUtility`, `Package.php` — not as the version the extension supports.

A grep of the answer for `runTests.sh`, `Build/Scripts` and Gerrit returns nothing. Every command and file named is this repository's own — `composer test`, `cgl:ci`, `test:php:lint`, `set-version`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `publish.yml`, `Build/Gruntfile.js` — and the CI finding is precisely that this project's own matrix does not execute this project's own declared range. The one thing brought in from outside is `UnitTests.xml`/`FunctionalTests.xml` and their bootstraps "from `typo3/testing-framework`", which is the package that ships them as templates and the source the skill names, not another extension's setup copied wholesale.

No file was changed and no tool that could change one was called. Four subjects that would have been easy headline findings are graded as what they are instead: the trailing comma in `ext_tables.sql` parses on 14.3 and is reported as not a defect after being test-parsed; `syntax_language` in `ext_tables.sql` is a column TCA already describes, named with "no consequence" because the schema analyzer derives it either way; `addTcaSelectItem` was checked against the changelog and found not deprecated, so finding 8 is "convention drift and a readability cost, not a break"; and the PHP 7.4 publish job works today. The one verdict that outruns its evidence is finding 2's "it renders empty in a clean install" — the evidence chain behind it is complete and each link was re-checked here, but the behaviour itself was reasoned about rather than reproduced, and the finding does not say so.

notes:
The third run of REVIEW-02 and the first in a checkout without complete static quality infrastructure. Session 41df06c7-58a1-4723-a367-52b823ed526c, 2026-07-31 12:21-12:28 CEST, seven minutes, one prompt and no steering. The run of 08:15 that this replaces is in commit 620eefd, judged `covered` against the same criteria digest in /home/benji/projects/bootstrap_package.

Setup. /home/benji/projects/syntax at dc94545, `bk2k/syntax` 5.0.0, TYPO3 14.3.0 below `.build/vendor`, declared range `^13.4 || ^14.3`, DDEV up. php-cs-fixer and phplint are configured and wired into CI; there is no PHPStan, no static analysis step, no baseline, and no `Tests/` directory at all although `autoload-dev` declares its namespace. That is what this checkout was chosen for. The server is not a Composer dependency there, so the skills were published from this checkout with `install --agent=claude` immediately before the run and `references/base.md` verified byte-identical to `skills/base.md`. 425 tests green.

All five criteria met and all four failures avoided, so `covered` a second time — but on a different repository, which is what makes the pair worth reading together. Against bootstrap_package's complete infrastructure the review read the baseline and the phpunit configurations rather than replacing them, and what it produced were verification gaps inside what exists. Here, where the infrastructure is half there, it produced finding 1: the matrix proves nothing beyond "the files parse". What it did **not** produce, in either run, is any statement about static analysis. There is no PHPStan in this repository and the review does not say so, does not scope one, and routes the whole of finding 1 to `typo3-extension-testing` — whose only sentence on the subject is that architecture or static checks are added when the project already uses them. So a missing static quality workflow surfaces as a missing **test** workflow, and the skill it lands in declines it by its own rule. That is the half the note was still owed.

What this run cost before it produced anything. Two earlier attempts at the same prompt in the same checkout died silently, 24 minutes apart: session ec7e020e at 11:36 after 80 tool calls, session 63b738bc at 12:11 after 92. Both stalled at the same juncture and neither reported an error. The cause was in this server, not the client: `Typo3Cli::execute()` gave `proc_open` no descriptor for fd 0, so a console command inherited the server's own stdin — which on the stdio transport is the client's request stream. `ddev exec` reads stdin to the end. The debug log of the second attempt has it exactly: `typo3_label_lookup` dispatched at 10:11:02.079 and answered in 350ms, `typo3_icon_lookup` dispatched at 10:11:02.361 while the first was still running, and then "still running" every 30 seconds forever. Every one of the twenty MCP calls before that pair had been strictly serial. Fixed in 88b7bb4 with `R-DIS-18` and a smoke test behind it, and this run is the first against the fixed server. It is worth recording that the console side of this server had never been under two concurrent calls outside E-SITE, and that the first extension review to reach for `typo3_icon_lookup` and `typo3_label_lookup` is the one that found it.

The run that then succeeded called no installation-backed tool at all: fifteen server calls, of which three are scope and guide, four architecture, six changelog and two documentation. DDEV was up and reachable for a third time in this environment without a question arising that needed it.

Judging notes for whoever reads this next. Eleven of the answer's claims were re-checked against the checkout and the installed core and all eleven hold, including four exact line numbers in `typo3/cms-core`. Two counts are arguable rather than wrong: `Build/Gruntfile.js` bundles eighteen `prismjs` component files where the answer says seventeen, which is right if `prism-core` is not counted as a language; and `typo3_extension_scope` reports `tests` and `manual` below `artifacts` rather than at the top level, where the answer quotes them from. No `<ide_opened_file>` attachment reached this session, unlike the 08:15 run.
